subject: Inference isolation visualization and CAIQ evidence
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@orchidfin.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
Cc: security@orchidfin.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Isolation visuals + CAIQ mapping for Private deployment

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you’re well. Orchid is preparing for a security review tied to an upcoming pilot where we plan to run PII-class workloads on Redwood Private. The audit team asked for a concise packet we can include in our vendor assessment:

- One consolidated network diagram that shows all isolation zones (control plane, inference/data plane, management), clear egress points, and where customer data is encrypted at rest/in transit.
- A short narrative (1–2 pages) mapping those diagram zones to CAIQ / SIG questions, and pointers to evidence artifacts (audit logs, KMS boundaries).
- Any standard mitigations you lean on for Dedicated vs Private (e.g., customer-managed VPC peering, routed NAT vs egress proxies, airgap patterns).

Can you provide a draft by Wednesday PST? Also tell me if you need an NDA/POC-level redaction for diagrams because of internal IP.

Thanks — Aisha
--
Aisha Patel
Senior Vendor Security Analyst
Orchid Financial
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@orchidfin.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Isolation visuals + CAIQ mapping for Private deployment

Aisha — thanks for the clear ask. We can do that. I’m attaching an initial visualization that annotates the three primary zones we use for Private deployments: Control Plane (customer-managed access controls and API endpoints), Inference Plane (GPU pools, KV-cache, model runtimes), and Management/Telemetry (logging, metrics, audit logs).

What I’m sending now is a redacted PNG of the topology and a short CAIQ mapping excerpt (see attachments). The items under attachments are intentionally high-level for the first pass; if Orchid needs IP-level callouts we can provide a separate classified packet under an NDA.

Proposed next steps:
- We’ll upload a draft CAIQ mapping to the Drive link below and link the JIRA with evidence placeholders (JIRA-SEC-4421).
- Jonas can provide a concise technical note describing how we enforce egress controls and per-customer KMS boundaries — that will cover the Dedicated vs Private differences.
- Schedule a 45-minute walkthrough (recommended) so we can walk your auditors through the diagram and call out log retention and packet-level evidence options.

I’m aiming to have the Drive doc and a 2-page narrative by end of day Wed PST. If that timeline is tight, let me know and we’ll move the walkthrough.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_inference_private_topology_v1.png (image/png)], [Attachment: CAIQ_network_mapping_excerpt.pdf (application/pdf)]

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security Architecture
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>, Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@orchidfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Isolation visuals + CAIQ mapping for Private deployment

Aisha / Kimberly — quick technical follow-up from my side. The attached figure Kim sent is a good starting point. A couple of clarifications I’ll include in the Drive doc:

1) Segmentation labels: we use three enforced boundaries in Private — Control Plane (mutually authenticated APIs over mTLS, customer-tied IAM roles), Inference/Data Plane (model runtime on isolated GPU nodes with prefix KV caching and read-only model artifacts), and Operations Plane (log collectors, metrics exporters, and management agents).
2) Egress policy options: for Private we typically offer (a) customer-managed peering with egress routing entirely in the customer VPC, (b) routed egress via our controlled NAT with per-customer firewall rules, or (c) a proxy/airlock pattern that permits only whitelisted egress endpoints. I’ll enumerate pros/cons in one table.
3) Evidence artifacts: we can supply (a) KMS key policy excerpts, (b) sample audit log slices (redacted), (c) ASH/Flow logs for a short time window, and (d) signed snapshots of model hash/versioning for provenance. If Orchid needs packet captures to demonstrate that management traffic never crosses the inference overlay, we’ll need a legal attestation — I’ll note that as optional.

I’ve created JIRA-SEC-4421 with tasks for each artifact and linked a Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB3cDefGHIjKlMnOpQ. I’ll upload the technical note and an annotated legend for the visualization by EOD tomorrow.

Jonas
Principal Network Architect
Redwood Inference

[Attachment reference: technical-note-segmentation.md (text/plain) — archived to Drive]
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@orchidfin.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Isolation visuals + CAIQ mapping for Private deployment

Kim, Jonas — this looks great, thank you.

Orchid would like the 45-minute walkthrough. Can you do Thursday 10am PST? We’ll have our vendor security lead (security@orchidfin.com) and one infra auditor on the call. A couple of notes before the meeting:

- Please mark any diagrams that expose internal hostnames or IPs as CONFIDENTIAL; we will treat those under our internal vendor NDA.
- For the CAIQ mapping, the audit team expects direct links to the evidence artifacts (even if redacted) — the Drive link you noted is perfect.
- If you can surface a short table that lists which artifacts are provided for Dedicated vs Private (explicitly calling out what’s identical vs what differs), that will speed approval.

Confirm Thursday 10am PST and we’ll send a calendar invite. Thanks again for the fast turnaround.

Best,
Aisha
